title: Defensive Programming
concept: Defensive programming means validating all inputs at system boundaries and using guard clauses to fail fast on invalid state.
why: Most security vulnerabilities come from unchecked inputs. Defensive programming catches invalid data at the earliest possible point.
tips: Validate at trust boundaries: user input, file I/O, network data, FFI calls
Guard clauses belong at the TOP of the function — fail before doing any work
Each guard should check ONE thing — compose them for layered defense
Return descriptive errors — the caller needs to know what to fix
common_mistakes: Validating input in the middle of the function after partial processing — fail early
Only validating format, not content (e.g., checking email has '@' but not checking domain validity)
Duplicating validation across multiple functions — validate at the boundary, trust internally
